page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384 is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 384 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1488.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a memory-to-core ratio of approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage. Additionally, it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With 384 dedicated vCPUs, this instance represents a high-density compute resource within the c4d family. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators represents a clear tradeoff, positioning the server primarily for non-graphical, CPU-bound workloads that rely on external storage systems. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density consolidates massive parallel processing power into a single virtual machine, reducing the overhead associated with managing multi-node clusters for large-scale compute tasks.

The balanced allocation of approximately 4 GB of RAM per vCPU makes this instance suitable for highly parallelized workloads. Appropriate use cases include large-scale web serving, high-throughput batch processing, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, and distributed data processing tasks that do not require local disk caching or GPU acceleration.
